lines.say: Cells are built from four big molecules: carbohydrates, lipids, proteins and nucleic acids.
Most are polymers. Think of carriages coupled onto a train.
Each time two join, one water molecule is released. That's condensation.

draw.alt: Carriages coupled, releasing water at each coupling

lines.say: Breaking a bond needs water added back. That's hydrolysis.
A chain of 150 amino acids has 149 bonds, so 149 waters are released.
Glucose forms a ring. The O H on carbon one points down in alpha, up in beta.
lines.write: α: OH down · β: OH up

lines.say: Sugars join by glycosidic bonds. Glucose plus fructose makes sucrose and water.
Alpha glucose makes starch and glycogen. The chain coils, compact for storage.
Beta glucose makes cellulose. Every second glucose flips, so the chain is straight.

draw.alt: Coiled starch chain versus straight cellulose chains linked by hydrogen bonds

lines.say: Straight chains hydrogen bond side by side into strong microfibrils.
Our enzymes only fit alpha bonds, so cellulose passes through as fibre.
Lipids are hydrophobic. They're mostly non polar C H bonds.
A triglyceride is glycerol plus three fatty acids, joined by ester bonds.
Saturated means straight means solid. Add a cis double bond, and the tail kinks.

draw.alt: Straight saturated tail and kinked unsaturated tail

lines.say: Phospholipids are amphipathic: a water loving head and two water fearing tails.
Steroids have four fused rings. Cholesterol sits in animal membranes.
Amino acids join by peptide bonds. The R group is what varies.
Primary structure is the order of beads on a necklace.

draw.alt: Amino acid beads in a chain

lines.say: Secondary is helices and sheets, held by hydrogen bonds in the backbone, not R groups.
Tertiary is the whole fold, held by R groups, including disulfide bridges.
Quaternary is several chains together, like haemoglobin's four subunits.
Denaturing loses the shape. The beads stay in order, the peptide bonds survive.
A nucleotide is a sugar, a phosphate and a base.
Phosphodiester bonds make a backbone running five prime to three prime.
DNA strands are antiparallel. A pairs with T, G pairs with C.

draw.alt: Two antiparallel strands with base pairs

lines.say: Pure As Gold. Purines are A and G, with two rings.
RNA uses ribose and uracil, and is usually single stranded.
Double stranded DNA is 22 percent adenine. So thymine is also 22.
A plus T is 44. So G plus C is 56.
Split it evenly. G is 28 percent and C is 28 percent.

draw.alt: Bar split into A 22, T 22, G 28, C 28

lines.say: More G C pairs means a higher melting temperature. They have three hydrogen bonds.
Lipids are not polymers. A triglyceride is glycerol plus three fatty acids.
Chargaff's rule only works for double stranded DNA.
In sickle cell, one amino acid changes. That alone changes the protein's behaviour.
Always name the bond: glycosidic, peptide, phosphodiester or ester.
